newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN JOBS SUMMIT PLANNED - LABOUR MINISTER.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN JOBS SUMMIT PLANNED - LABOUR MINISTER.

text.p: South Africa's deep-rooted unemployment problems would be the focus of a Presidential Jobs Summit to be held later this year, Labour Minister Tito Mboweni said on Monday.

"It is hoped that at this summit, government together with the social partners will commit themselves to specific actions intended to promote employment in a manner that is quantitatively and qualitatively different from what has been the case so far," Mboweni said.
Opening the parliamentary debate on his 1997/98 budget vote, Mboweni said discussions at the summit would be based on an employment strategy now being finalised.
Around a third of South Africa's workforce is unemployed.

The aim of the summit, which had been recommended by the Labour Market Commission, would be to thrash out an Accord for Employment and Growth that would commit government, business and labour to stabilising prices, wages and other economic indicators and to developmental initiatives at national and regional levels.

He said it was "quite erroneous" to believe that the task of creating jobs was the task of his ministry alone. Instead, it required the participation of government as a whole as well as the public and private sectors and organised labour.
This was because of the fragmented nature of the labour market as well as inherited labour market inefficiencies and inequalities.

Mboweni said that his department planned to present three new bills to parliament this year which would cover employment and occupational equity, basic conditions of employment and national skills development.
